problems.title: Multiply units digits
problems.question: Find the last digit of 2²·3³·7⁴·13⁶.
steps: The units digits are 4,7,1,9 respectively.
Their product is 252, ending in 2.

problems.title: Exterior angles of a convex polygon
problems.question: Find the sum of one exterior angle at each vertex of a convex polygon.
problems.idea: A walk around the polygon turns through one full rotation.
steps: The exterior sum is n·180°-(n-2)180°.
This equals 360° for every n≥3.

problems.title: A disguised square divided by a cube
problems.question: Simplify $\dfrac{a^{-2n}+b^{-2n}-2a^{-n}b^{-n}}{a^{-3n}-b^{-3n}-3a^{-n}b^{-n}(a^{-n}-b^{-n})}(a^n-b^n)$.
steps: The fraction is (u-v)²/(u-v)³=1/(u-v).
Also u-v=(bⁿ-aⁿ)/(aⁿbⁿ), so multiplying by aⁿ-bⁿ gives -aⁿbⁿ.
Retain the original domain: all powers must exist, a,b≠0 and a⁻ⁿ≠b⁻ⁿ.

problems.title: Two numbers around a round square
problems.question: Compute 2001·1999.
steps: The product is 2000²-1.

problems.title: Convert a difference-over-sum ratio
problems.question: If (a-b)/(a+b)=1/2, find (a²-b²)/(a²+b²), with the stated nonzero denominators.
problems.idea: Solve the simple proportional equation first.
steps: Substitute a=3b into the requested ratio.
It becomes (9b²-b²)/(9b²+b²)=8/10=0.8.

problems.title: When four bisector points are cyclic
problems.question: Internal bisectors AA₁,BB₁ meet at K. What condition makes A₁CB₁K cyclic?
formulas: AKB=90°+C/2; cyclic opposite angles sum to 180°.
steps: The rays KA₁,KB₁ are opposite KA,KB, so A₁KB₁=90°+C/2.
The opposite quadrilateral angle at C is C. Thus C+90°+C/2=180°.
Solve to get C=60°. The same calculation proves sufficiency.
problems.note: This does not require the whole triangle to be equilateral or acute; C=60° is the precise condition.

problems.title: Proportional ratios versus reciprocal sums
problems.question: Given a/b=c/d, |a|>|b|,|c|>|d| and all four nonzero, which listed derived identity may fail?
problems.idea: Ratio identities survive scaling, but reciprocal sums generally do not.
steps: Adding or subtracting 1 and taking valid reciprocal ratios gives the usual true proportion identities.
But (a+b)/(ab)=1/a+1/b need not equal 1/c+1/d.
For a=2,b=1,c=4,d=2, the original ratios are both 2, but the reciprocal sums are 3/2 and 3/4.
problems.answer: The identity (a+b)/(ab)=(c+d)/(cd) may be false (choice ე).

problems.title: A polyline has one fewer edge than vertices
problems.question: What is the greatest number of crossings between a line and an open polyline A₁…A₅₀?
problems.idea: Count segments, then arrange alternating vertices on opposite sides.
formulas: 50 vertices give 49 edges; a noncollinear segment meets a line at most once.
steps: Thus at most 49 separate crossings occur.
Alternating vertices across the line and choosing distinct crossing locations attains 49.
problems.note: If an edge is allowed to lie on the line, their intersection contains infinitely many points. The finite crossing question assumes no shared segment.

problems.title: Sum seven parallel sections
problems.question: A right triangle’s hypotenuse is divided into eight equal parts. Through the seven division points draw segments parallel to the 8 cm leg until the other leg. Find their length sum.
problems.idea: Similarity makes section lengths proportional to their distance from the vertex.
steps: The seven lengths are 1,2,3,4,5,6,7 cm.
Their sum is 7·8/2=28 cm.

problems.title: Midpoint of the hypotenuse between two bisectors
problems.question: Parallelogram ABCD has AB=6.2,BC=8. The A,D bisectors meet at O and cut BC at F,E. K is the midpoint of FE. Find OK.
formulas: BF=AB,CE=CD; a right-triangle hypotenuse midpoint is equidistant from all vertices.
steps: O lies on the two bisectors, making EOF a right triangle.
K is its hypotenuse midpoint, so OK=EF/2=2.2.

problems.title: A rectangle diagonal’s perpendicular bisector
problems.question: The perpendicular bisector of diagonal KM meets rectangle sides KL,MN at A,B. Given AB=BM=6.8, find its longer side.
steps: Perpendicularity gives w(w-2t)+h²=0. Also AB²=(w-2t)²+h²=t².
Eliminate h² to obtain 4t²-2wt=t², hence w=3t/2=10.2. The other side is √3t/2, which is shorter.

problems.title: A diameter condition fixes the side ratio
problems.question: A circle with diameter AD passes through the midpoint M of BC in parallelogram ABCD. Its perimeter is 12.6. Find the shorter side.
problems.idea: Use the right angle subtending a diameter.
steps: Let u=AD and v=AB. The midpoint M has vector v+u/2.
AM⊥DM gives |AB|²=|AD|²/4, so AD=2AB.
The perimeter is 2(AB+2AB)=6AB=12.6.

problems.title: An exact interval for a linear expression
problems.question: If 2<a<5 and -3<b<-1, find the range of 3a-2b.
problems.idea: Scale each interval, reversing bounds when multiplying by a negative number.
steps: Add bounds to get 8<3a-2b<21.
Independent continuous a,b attain every intermediate value, but neither endpoint.

problems.title: A rational root and its interval
problems.question: Solve 2x/(x²+3x)-1/x=0 and identify its listed interval.
problems.idea: Keep x=0,-3 out of the domain.
steps: 2/(x+3)=1/x gives 2x=x+3, hence x=3.
It is valid and lies in (2.2,3.4).

problems.title: A cancelled square expression
problems.question: Simplify [4x²+y²-(2x-y)²]/(2xy).
steps: The numerator reduces to 4xy.
Divide by 2xy to get 2, with x,y≠0.

problems.title: Repeated difference of squares
problems.question: Simplify (a+b)(a²+b²)(a⁴+b⁴)(a⁸+b⁸).
problems.idea: Multiply by a-b to see the telescoping pattern.
steps: Successive multiplication by a-b produces a²-b², then a⁴-b⁴, a⁸-b⁸, and a¹⁶-b¹⁶.
For a≠b, the product is (a¹⁶-b¹⁶)/(a-b).
At a=b the original product remains defined and equals 16a¹⁵.
problems.answer: $(a^{16}-b^{16})/(a-b)$ if a≠b; at a=b it equals 16a¹⁵.

problems.title: Factor before substituting close decimals
problems.question: Evaluate [(a²-ab)/(a²-b²)]·[16/(a²+ab)] at a=1.99,b=0.01.
problems.idea: The factors a and a-b cancel.
steps: The product simplifies to 16/(a+b)² on its domain.
Here a+b=2, so its value is 16/4=4.

problems.title: A cyclic trapezoid with a 90-degree leg chord
problems.question: A cyclic trapezoid’s leg subtends 90° at its circumcentre. Its midline is 12.6 cm. Find its height.
problems.idea: The equal legs make the trapezoid isosceles; a quarter-turn separates the leg endpoints on the circle.
formulas: For right-side endpoints at angles u,v: midline=R(cosu+cosv), height=R(sinu-sinv).
steps: The 90° central angle gives u-v=90°. Thus cosu=-sinv and sinu=cosv.
Both height and midline then equal R(cosv-sinv).
Hence the height equals the given midline.

problems.title: Odd congruence classes make the final subtraction redundant
problems.question: A contains two-digit multiples of 9, B even integers, C integers with remainder 3 modulo 4. Find |(A∩C)\B|.
formulas: An integer congruent to 3 modulo 4 is odd.
steps: None is even, so removing B deletes nothing.

problems.title: A circle centre and a leg midpoint
problems.question: A tangential trapezoid has bases BC,AD. CK⊥AD, O is the incircle centre, M the midpoint of CD. Given OKM=58°, find OMK.
formulas: Incircle diameter=height h; midpoint of a right-triangle hypotenuse is equidistant from its vertices.
steps: O and M both lie at height h/2, so OM∥AD. In right triangle CDK, MK=CD/2.
Writing d as the horizontal projection of CD and l=CD, the D-angle bisector locates O at horizontal distance (l+d)/2 from D. This gives OM=l/2 as well.
Thus angles MOK and OKM are both 58°. The remaining angle OMK is 180°-116°=64°.

problems.title: Factor a power difference
problems.question: How many times larger than 600 is 5¹⁰-5⁸?
steps: The ratio is 24·5⁸/(24·25).
Cancel to obtain 5⁶.

problems.title: Cancel negative powers
problems.question: Simplify $[(ax)^{-2}/(by)^3]\,[(abx)^2/y^{-3}]$.
formulas: (uv)ⁿ=uⁿvⁿ; division by y⁻³ multiplies by y³.
steps: The product is a⁻²x⁻²b⁻³y⁻³·a²b²x²y³.
All powers cancel except b⁻¹. Keep a,b,x,y nonzero.

problems.title: Cancel denominators without losing the restriction
problems.question: Solve (x-2)/(3x+9)=(2x²-9)/[6(x²+6x+9)].
steps: Multiply by 6(x+3)² to get 2(x-2)(x+3)=2x²-9.
Expand and cancel: 2x-12=-9.
Thus x=3/2, which is allowed.

problems.title: Reciprocal symmetry
problems.question: P(b)=(b+3/b)(3b+1/b), b≠0. Find P(b)/P(1/b).
steps: Replacing b by 1/b exchanges the first and last terms.
Thus P(1/b)=P(b)>0, so the quotient is 1.

problems.title: A midpoint rectangle inside a rhombus
problems.question: A rhombus has inradius 3.6 and acute angle 30°. Find the circumcircle diameter of its side-midpoint quadrilateral.
problems.idea: The midpoint quadrilateral is a rectangle whose diagonal equals the rhombus side.
formulas: Rhombus height=2r=s sinα; a rectangle’s circumdiameter is its diagonal.
steps: The rhombus side is s=7.2/sin30°=14.4.
Its midpoint rectangle has sides half the two perpendicular rhombus diagonals. Their squared lengths add to s².
Thus its diagonal, and circumdiameter, equal s.
